content.tex: B MODELLING BODY MASS (20 marks)
You are advised to spend no more than 45 minutes on this part.
This task looks at three different models for the approximate body mass of an adult.

parts.text: Here is a simple model to calculate the approximate body mass of an adult. Measure the height in centimetres and subtract 100 to get the approximate mass in kilograms.

content.tex: Here is a simple model to calculate the approximate body mass of an adult.
Measure the height in centimetres and subtract 100 to get the approximate mass in kilograms.
Find the approximate body mass of an adult who is \(1.8m\) tall.

parts.text: In the 19 th century, the Belgian mathematician Quetelet suggested a different model. In his model the approximate body mass of an adult, M kg, varies as the square of the height, h metres. For an adult with height 2 m the approximate body mass is 88 kg.

content.tex: In the \(19^{th}\) century, the Belgian mathematician Quetelet suggested a different model.
In his model the approximate body mass of an adult, \(M\) kg, varies as the square of the height, \(h\) metres. For an adult with height \(2m\) the approximate body mass is 88kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Show that Quetelet’s model can be written as M = 22 h 2 .

content.tex: Show that Quetelet’s model can be written as \(M = 22h^{2}\) .
